newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch PTT calls for probe into phoney bid.
newsitem.headline: Dutch PTT calls for probe into phoney bid.

text.p: Dutch post and telecoms group PTT Nederland NV said on Wednesday it would ask the Dutch authorities to investigate an attempt to forge documents purporting to represent a take-over bid from the group.

A PTT spokesman said the company was offended to learn that the Finnish city of Turku had received a fake fax that had been made to look like a bid from the Dutch group's PTT Telecom unit for the city's telephone operator Turun Puhelin.
"We take this as an attack on the integrity of the company and will try to identify the person responsible," spokesman Ernst Moeksis told Reuters.
"We will inform the Dutch police and the justice authorities and see what they can do about the matter," he added.
The city of Turku was forced to delay the privatisation of the telephone operator on Monday after a fax was received which at first glance seemed to announce a bid from Dutch PTT.
The bogus bid was higher than the real bids and was based on documents which, an adviser to the city said, "could be easily obtained via the Internet".
But it was subsequently discovered that the fax was an elaborate hoax.
Moeksis said Dutch PTT denied it was the source of the fax when Turku city officials called the Dutch group to verify its interest on Tuesday.
He said the fax contained a logo that was similar to Dutch PTT's, adding that it could easily be obtained from Dutch PTT's various Internet sites and then manipulated.
There was nothing the company could do to percent such sophisticated hoax attempts, he added.
